In my view, companies should be allowed to share customer data with partners, but only under strict conditions. The main benefit is that partners can understand their customers better. For example, if a retailer knows which products are popular in each store, it can plan its stock more efficiently and offer more relevant deals. That said, I acknowledge that privacy is a valid concern. Many people worry that their personal details might be sold or misused, and those fears are not unreasonable. However, I'd argue that the risk can be mitigated. Data can be anonymised, so no individual can be identified, and it can be encrypted and stored securely. In my own work, for instance, we share only anonymised monthly reports with our retail partner, and no customer names are ever included. So, on balance, I don't think a total ban is necessary.
